capture.final_message:
Use the edge-set representation of simple graphs and prove the two conjuncts separately.

For the first conjunct, apply graph extensionality and fix vertices \(v,w\). Adjacency in `fromEdgeSet s` is equivalent to \(\{v,w\}\in s\) together with the loop-free condition \(v\ne w\). Then:

- membership in `Set.iInter f` becomes `∀ i, Sym2.mk v w ∈ f i`;
- adjacency in the infimum becomes adjacency in every `fromEdgeSet (f i)`;
- the common condition \(v\ne w\) can be moved across the universal quantifier. The empty-index case is handled automatically: both sides give the complete simple graph.

For the second conjunct, unfold `incidenceSet`: it consists of graph edges incident to \(v\). The edge `Sym2.mk v w` is automatically incident to \(v\), so membership reduces to its membership in `G.edgeSet`, which is precisely `G.Adj v w`.

Thus the main intermediate goals are the adjacency characterization of `fromEdgeSet`, adjacency in an `iInf`, membership in an indexed intersection, and the edge-set characterization of adjacency.
